issues.legal_issue: The acquired disputed and adjacent land must remain in its existing status, without religious activity or transfer, until the pending title suits are decided.
material_facts: The acquisition covered both the disputed site and adjacent land, and the adjacent land’s necessary use depended on which side prevailed in the title litigation.
The acquired land had remained in its existing condition for many years, and the pending suits were approaching final stages.
The court had earlier ordered that religious activity on the acquired land was not permitted and that the land was to be retained pending the proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The earlier status quo order, as modified, was to remain operative until disposal of the pending suits, including the prohibition on religious activity on the acquired land.
issues.legal_principle: Under the Acquisition of Certain Area at Ayodhya Act, 1993, particularly Sections 6 and 7, the disputed area was held by the Central Government as a statutory receiver for management and eventual handover according to the suits’ outcome, while adjacent land was acquired to make the outcome effective and any area later found superfluous was to be restored. Applying M. Ismail Faruqui v. Union of India, the Court held that the disputed and adjacent areas were intrinsically connected at this stage and that their use depended on the final adjudication. Preserving the existing condition protected the ability to grant effective relief and supported the Act’s objectives of public order and communal harmony.

rule.if: public_interest_writ_concerns_acquired_land and title_suits_are_pending and disputed_and_adjacent_land_are_interdependent and status_quo_has_long_been_maintained and suits_are_nearing_disposition

predicates.public_interest_writ_concerns_acquired_l: A public-interest writ proceeding concerns land acquired in connection with a disputed site.
predicates.title_suits_are_pending: Title suits concerning the disputed site remain pending before a court.
predicates.disputed_and_adjacent_land_are_interdepe: The use of adjacent acquired land depends on the outcome of the title dispute over the central site.
predicates.status_quo_has_long_been_maintained: The acquired land has remained in an established condition for a substantial period during the dispute.
predicates.suits_are_nearing_disposition: The pending title suits are approaching final adjudication.

issues.definition: When a public-interest writ concerns acquired land whose disputed and adjacent portions depend on pending, nearly concluded title suits, and the existing condition has long been maintained, the land remains without religious activity or transfer until those suits are disposed of.

issues.legal_issue: A public-interest petition concerning the preservation of acquired land during pending title litigation is not barred merely because a related petition was earlier dismissed or because the initial pleadings are challenged as inadequate.
material_facts: A writ petition concerning the acquired land had previously been filed in a High Court and dismissed.
The present proceeding concerned maintaining the existing condition of acquired land while title suits remained pending, a scope the Court found different from that of the earlier petition.
The Supreme Court had issued notice, other interested parties had been impleaded, and pleadings had developed before the matter was considered.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to dismiss the petition on the basis of the earlier High Court proceeding or the objections to the petition’s pleadings, and considered the matter on its merits.
issues.legal_principle: In public-interest proceedings, the Court does not adopt an unduly technical or narrow approach to pleadings, particularly after notice has issued, interested parties have been joined, and the issues have been developed. An earlier petition does not preclude consideration where the later proceeding raises a different issue.

rule.if: public_interest_proceeding and earlier_petition_was_dismissed and present_proceeding_has_a_different_scope and interested_parties_have_been_heard

predicates.public_interest_proceeding: The matter is brought as a public-interest proceeding.
predicates.earlier_petition_was_dismissed: An earlier petition concerning related subject matter was dismissed by another court.
predicates.present_proceeding_has_a_different_scope: The present proceeding raises an issue distinct from the issue raised in the earlier petition.
predicates.interested_parties_have_been_heard: Interested parties have been joined and given an opportunity to present their positions.

issues.definition: When a public-interest proceeding has a different scope from an earlier dismissed petition and interested parties have been heard, the present petition is not dismissed solely because of that earlier proceeding or initial pleading objections.
